text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- British lawyers may clash in Malawi's Supreme Court if the government instructs one to face fellow British lawyer Clive Stanbrook, who is defending former president Kamuzu Banda charged with allegedly plotting to murder four senior politicians in 1983.
- Water and Irrigation Ministry officials say they fear that persistent rainfall in southern Malawi may cause more flooding.

- American multi-national soft drinks manufacturer Pepsi Cola is close to completing plans to open a 165 million kwacha ($11 million) plant in Blantyre with Malawi Development Corporation as a joint partner.

- Four opposition political parties have called for Chief Justice Richard Banda to step down after claims that he approached a High Court judge to rule in favour of the government in a case involving the opposition Malawi Congress Party.
- Leader of the Muslim Sect-Kadalia was arrested on Thursday for allegedly denouncing President Bakili Muluzi, also a Moslem of another sect, while preaching in a mosque.
